Its Bloch vector is \(\tanh(2tg/T)(1/g,0,-q/g)\), and the exact single-qubit stabilizer octahedron yields the if-and-only-if thermal criterion. Strict temperature monotonicity, the explicit derivative \(L'(q)=(q-1)/(2qg)\), and asymptotic expansions establish uniqueness, monotonicity, and limits; the exact reciprocal duality follows from invariance of the encoded octahedron ratio under interaction inversion. value.rationale: The motivating work numerically identifies a physically meaningful critical temperature and its eigenstate-mixing mechanism but leaves its continuous phase boundary without an exact classification. The theorem gives an explicit and unique critical temperature for every repulsive interaction, strict invertibility, two sharp coupling regimes linked by an exact reciprocal interaction identity, and exponentially small low-temperature critical interaction. The Pauli postselection result explains why thermally populated auxiliary stabilizer levels cannot alter the threshold. These exact complete boundary facts are a motivated quantum-resource diagnostic rather than an arbitrary small-case table or generic substitution; they make the entire plotted phase contour analytically reproducible. Limits: canonical two-electron sector only, not full robustness away from the zero boundary.
